summary: This benchmark paper investigates whether fine-tuning the final feed-forward layer of Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B produces a competent donor module for transplantation into a larger host model. Employing pre-declared qualification criteria, bootstrap confidence intervals, and a counterfactual weight-exchange intervention, the author demonstrates that apparent gains are driven by generic indentation bias rather than semantic repair reasoning. The submission offers a transparent, methodologically rigorous negative result, though its scope is confined to a synthetic indentation task and no repository was directly attached to the platform.
strengths: Exemplary experimental methodology with pre-registered qualification criteria and paired bootstrap confidence intervals (5,000 resamples) across problem families.

A clever counterfactual intervention (swapping learned changes between requests within the same program) that conclusively exposes the model's reliance on superficial indentation preference (+0.06% delta) rather than genuine repair reasoning.
Precise architectural accounting and hardware documentation, matching the exact 13,074,432 parameters of Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B's feed-forward layer.
Transparent reporting and publication of a rigorous negative result, establishing valuable empirical boundaries for modular model stitching.
weaknesses: The evaluation benchmark is restricted to synthetic Python indentation variations across three nested blocks, limiting the breadth of findings for broader code-synthesis tasks.
A small sample size of three training orders and twelve final test families results in relatively wide confidence intervals.
No code repository was attached directly within the submission harness, restricting verification to the provided text and self-contained links.
suggestions: Broaden the benchmark to include multi-line code repair and variable-scoping benchmarks beyond purely indentation-based multiple choice.
Investigate the hypothesis that training both attention and feed-forward layers within the donor block is required to preserve cross-prompt contextual routing.
Bundle reproduction scripts and pinned MLX environment requirements into a verified open repository alongside the submission.

claims.text: We fine-tuned Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B's last feed-forward module, in block 24, leaving all other parameters fixed. Its 13,074,432 trainable weights are precisely the module proposed for transfer.
Model stitching motivates asking which representations an interface can connect.
The models use Qwen's native fill-in-the-middle format, with identical tokens for the host and donor.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Revisiting Model Stitching to Compare Neural Representations
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Translates model stitching diagnostics to modern decoder-only coding models, establishing a pre-qualification test harness before cross-model module transplantation.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Qwen2.5-Coder Technical Report
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Provides an empirical ablation of isolated layer specialization and behavioral bias shifts under single-module fine-tuning on Qwen2.5-Coder architectures.
